entries.title: Python 3.15 adds lazy imports and new runtime capabilities
entries.summary: Python 3.15 introduces lazy imports, immutable frozendict objects and sentinel support, while making UTF-8 the default encoding. These changes offer new options for scientific applications, but teams should check dependencies and encoding assumptions before migrating; the JIT remains experimental.

entries.title: October certificate and runtime security updates affect Python environments
entries.summary: Python 3.15.2 distrusts compromised certificate-authority keys and fixes tarfile filtering, following an earlier update to bundled pip and certifi. Related October releases of uv, Snakemake and Quarto update affected trust components or runtimes, making pinned analysis environments and workflow containers worth reviewing.
entries.source: Python and official project release notes

entries.title: R 4.6.2 fixes constrained optimization and large-count sampling
entries.summary: R 4.6.2 fixes a compiler-related problem in constrained nlminb optimization and prevents integer overflow in rhyper when population counts exceed the integer limit. These numerical fixes matter for reproducible statistical analyses even though this is a patch release.

entries.title: renv 1.3.1 improves concurrent cache use and restoration checks
entries.summary: renv 1.3.1 addresses concurrent cache races and cross-filesystem installation handling, and warns when a retrieved package does not match the requested package. Restoration and system-requirement fixes help make shared R environments more dependable.

entries.title: uv 0.13 changes Python defaults and hash-checking behavior
entries.summary: uv 0.13 selects Python 3.15 when an unpinned environment needs a default interpreter and changes hash checking for constrained dependencies. Its cache-format change can require rebuilding cached artifacts, so reproducible workflows should specify interpreter versions and review lock/install behavior.

entries.title: Nextflow 26.10 updates workflow controls and fixes credential exposure
entries.summary: Nextflow 26.10 adds resource-limit handling and workflow typing improvements while deprecating process-level when conditions in favor of configuration-based controls. The October 26.10.3 and 25.10.9 security fixes prevent Bitbucket Cloud tokens from appearing in repository URLs and logs; affected users should follow the release guidance on token rotation.

entries.title: RStudio 2026.10 adds Git worktrees and higher-resolution plot export
entries.summary: RStudio 2026.10 adds Git worktree workflows and fixed-size plot export with resolution options up to 600 DPI. Improved source diagnostics and atomic state-file writes support analysis development and more reliable IDE sessions.

entries.title: Positron October release expands assistant access to the IDE
entries.summary: Positron adds assistant tools that can interact with the IDE, alongside data-connection and Quarto workflow improvements. An experimental MCP server exposes IDE capabilities to other agents, so teams evaluating integrations should distinguish this preview interface from established editor features.

entries.title: VS Code October updates expand remote and agent workflows
entries.summary: VS Code 1.141–1.144 add terminal sandboxing and worktree management, expand agent controls, and connect local development with cloud tasks. Some assistance features depend on Copilot plans or enterprise policy, while computer-use and on-device model features remain experimental.

entries.title: GPT-6.1 Terra becomes available in Codex and ChatGPT Work
entries.summary: OpenAI made GPT-6.1 Terra available for coding and computer-interaction work in Codex and ChatGPT Work on eligible Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu plans. This is Work/Codex availability, rather than general Chat availability; organizational controls and the stated UAE data-residency restriction still apply.
entries.claims: Product capabilities and availability are vendor-reported.

entries.title: Codex CLI October updates strengthen permission handling and integrations
entries.summary: Codex CLI 0.164–0.166 add reusable presets and a Vertex provider, improve credential masking, and validate marketplace URLs. Permission preservation across resumed or forked sessions and new network diagnostics are relevant to controlled, reproducible agent-assisted development.

entries.title: Claude Code October updates tighten write and sandbox boundaries
entries.summary: Claude Code adds a setting that blocks writes outside configured working directories across permission modes, alongside protections for shell startup files, symlinks and MCP configuration. These October changes help teams define safer boundaries for coding agents working with analysis projects; their behavior still depends on configured permissions.

entries.title: Quarto 1.11 improves accessible outputs and updates its runtime
entries.summary: Quarto 1.11 improves accessible document output, including alternative text handling for DOCX figures and Mermaid diagrams. Its runtime update also changes compatibility requirements, including macOS 12 or later, so teams maintaining automated reports should review deployment environments before upgrading.

entries.title: Scanpy 1.12.5 preserves the gene symbol nan during import
entries.summary: Scanpy 1.12.5 stops treating the literal gene symbol nan as a missing value when reading 10x matrix data. It also supports pynndescent 0.7 in neighbor construction and ingest, making this patch relevant to annotation integrity and dependency compatibility.

entries.title: Ruff 0.17 changes Python defaults and signs distributed binaries
entries.summary: Ruff 0.17 introduces signed macOS and Windows binaries and updates its default Python target and lint rules. Projects without an explicit target version now default to Python 3.11, so scientific teams should pin configuration to avoid unexpected CI or autofix changes.

entries.title: Polars 2.0 expands out-of-core analysis and corrects SQL behavior
entries.summary: Polars 2.0 enables out-of-core execution by default and expands SQL window and Decimal handling. It also corrects analytical-query edge cases and changes APIs, making migration checks important for pipelines that depend on precise types, ordering and numerical results.

entries.title: DuckDB 2.0 LTS adds remote access and asynchronous I/O
entries.summary: DuckDB 2.0 LTS expands the Quack remote protocol, asynchronous I/O and support for heterogeneous data through a first-class VARIANT type. Support runs through at least October 2027, but analytical applications should review the documented breaking changes before moving existing workflows.

entries.title: Pillow 13 fixes image-processing vulnerabilities and drops Python 3.10
entries.summary: Pillow 13 addresses multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in image processing and decoding. It also drops Python 3.10 support and removes silent clipping when saving I-mode images as PNG, changes that matter for secure and faithful scientific-image workflows.

entries.title: Shiny for Python 1.9 makes asynchronous outputs concurrent
entries.summary: Shiny for Python 1.9 runs asynchronous effects and outputs concurrently, preventing one slow await from holding up other outputs or sessions. Background-task UI updates and accessibility improvements help interactive research applications, while existing apps should be checked for assumptions about effect execution order.

entries.title: nf-core/tools 4.2 guidance covers template migration and CI security
entries.summary: The nf-core/tools 4.2 announcement explains pipeline diagrams, regenerating container configuration and migrating GPU settings to Nextflow accelerator directives. It also documents a reusable lint-workflow token leak fix and template synchronization corrections, making the post useful for pipeline maintainers.
entries.eligibility_note: October 21 blog publication; not an assertion that both release tags were published that day.

entries.title: CellDiffusion integrates single-cell studies using graph diffusion
entries.summary: CellDiffusion learns relationships among cells to correct batch effects while preserving cell-type structure and trajectories. RNA-seq Blog covers the October 16 Science Advances paper, whose evaluations include human endometrium data; reported performance remains specific to the tested datasets.
entries.access: Blog and primary author abstract via Europe PMC

entries.title: SpliceCOV filters transcriptional noise before transcript assembly
entries.summary: SpliceCOV uses annotated splice and transcript-boundary features to filter noisy RNA-seq alignments before StringTie assembly. RNA-seq Blog covers the October 20 Genes paper, which reports improved precision in GTEx comparisons but weaker transfer to mouse data, highlighting the importance of organism-specific validation.
entries.access: Blog and primary author abstract via Europe PMC

entries.title: RNAmel provides reproducible bulk RNA-seq analysis in Shiny
entries.summary: RNAmel combines bulk RNA-seq differential expression, co-expression and gene-set analysis in an R/Shiny interface. Exportable R scripts and HTML reports expose the analysis steps and dependencies, with reproducibility evaluated on two published datasets.
entries.access: Primary paper; blog posting date unresolved, eligibility established by paper.

entries.title: DeCoRE resolves RNA conformations using direct RNA sequencing
entries.summary: DeCoRE combines RNA structure probing with direct RNA sequencing signals to separate alternative structural conformations. Demonstrations on riboswitches and bacterial ribosomal RNA suggest a route to studying structural heterogeneity, with conclusions limited to the evaluated experimental systems.
entries.access: Primary author abstract via Europe PMC; October 6 blog date seen in tag search but not independently established, so paper date used.

entries.title: CCI-seq connects cell proximity with molecular states
entries.summary: CCI-seq combines indexing of cell clumps with single-cell sequencing to identify proximity networks and associated molecular states. Applications in mouse tissues and human colorectal cancer show how it can complement transcriptomic studies of tissue and tumor microenvironments.

entries.title: Recordanelles preserve earlier transcriptional states in living cells
entries.summary: Engineered recordanelles capture endogenous messenger RNA over time, allowing earlier transcriptional states to be read alongside current single-cell profiles. Demonstrations in human cells include transient interferon responses, offering an experimental approach to cellular history rather than an established clinical assay.

entries.title: scMagnify infers dynamic regulatory programs from single-cell multiomics
entries.summary: scMagnify integrates single-cell multiomic measurements to infer regulatory modules and their temporal relationships. Applications to hematopoiesis, pancreas development and kidney injury illustrate hypothesis generation, while inferred regulatory direction should not be mistaken for experimental proof of causality.

entries.title: Single-cell chromatin QTL resource links immune variation to disease loci
entries.summary: A large peripheral-blood single-cell chromatin study maps genetic effects across immune cell types and states. Integrating chromatin and expression QTL evidence helps prioritize regulatory mechanisms at disease-associated loci, providing a resource for follow-up rather than direct evidence of causality.

entries.title: GIAB HG002 benchmark expands variant evaluation in difficult regions
entries.summary: This preprint presents an assembly-based HG002 benchmark that extends small- and structural-variant evaluation into repetitive and previously difficult genomic regions. Separate and combined benchmark sets across reference assemblies provide resources for validating sequencing pipelines; the curated manuscript is a preprint.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: The Genome In A Bottle HG002 assembly-based variant benchmark set enables comprehensive benchmarking of small and structural variants.

entries.title: Matched 10x and Parse comparisons reveal platform-dependent RNA profiles
entries.summary: This preprint compares seven matched sample pairs from five studies and separates priming-related biases from larger platform-level differences between 10x and Parse. Reported differences in nuclear RNA representation and comparable background contamination caution against treating measurements as interchangeable; the study focuses on gene counts and composition rather than a universal platform ranking.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: A Unified Comparison of 10X Genomics and Parse Biosciences scRNA-seq Technologies

entries.title: Spatial transcriptomics benchmark compares capture and spatial accuracy
entries.summary: This preprint compares sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics platforms across tissue types and preservation methods, examining capture architecture, capture efficiency and spatial accuracy. Its proposed operational metrics may help experimental planning, but performance remains dependent on the tested assays and specimens.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: Navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technologies: a comprehensive multi-platform benchmark

entries.title: Spatial RNA and protein measurements can imply different tumor biology
entries.summary: This preprint compares paired RNA and protein measurements for 21 targets in lung and prostate cancer specimens. Marker-dependent agreement and divergent spatial patterns, including for several checkpoint molecules, support orthogonal protein validation before interpreting spatial RNA as a protein proxy.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: RNA and protein are not interchangeable in single-cell spatial multi-omics

entries.title: EL-PERTURB tests perturbation models outside their training distribution
entries.summary: This preprint evaluates 20 perturbation prediction models using functionally separated training and test sets. Performance deteriorated under these harder conditions, with complex architectures offering no consistent advantage over simpler baselines in the reported comparisons, emphasizing realistic validation before substituting predictions for experiments.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: Genetic Perturbation Prediction Models Fail Out-of-Distribution: A Rigorous Benchmark and Systematic Evaluation

entries.title: Ambient RNA correction can conceal doublets in single-cell analysis
entries.summary: This preprint evaluates ambient RNA correction and doublet detection using engineered and multiplexed datasets. Doublet detection generally worked better before decontX or SoupX correction, with CellBender an exception, suggesting that preprocessing order should be validated rather than assumed interchangeable.
entries.access: Official API author abstract only; no full manuscript review

version_history.title: Order Matters: Ambient RNA correction confounds doublet detection in single-cell RNA sequencing

entries.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 adds adjustable effort for high-volume AI tasks
entries.summary: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 with adjustable effort and lower published pricing for high-volume tasks such as classification, summarization and coding subagents. It is available through the Claude Platform and supported cloud providers; performance and cost comparisons in the announcement are vendor claims, not independent biomedical validation.

coverage_lessons: Enumerate bioRxiv interval pages before relying on search: 1,585 version records required 55 requests; date-like DOI prefixes did not match posting dates.
Compare abstracts and underlying developments across DOIs. A different DOI is not sufficient evidence of a new study; keep uncertain lineage unresolved.
